newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco marijuana club to reopen.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco marijuana club to reopen.

text.p: A San Francisco club that sold marijuana to the sick until closed by authorities five months ago will reopen next week following a court ruling on Wednesday, its founder said on Wednesday.

San Francisco Superior Court Judge David Garcia said he would modify an injunction that shut the San Francisco Cannabis Buyers' Club to allow the club to grow marijuana for medicinal uses approved by a doctor. He made a tentative ruling in court and must still issue a final order.
The change followed the passage of a measure by California voters in November allowing sick people legally to use marijuana to ease the pain of illnesses such as AIDS, cancer and glaucoma.

The club used to sell marijuana to about 12,000 people the club said suffered from serious illness. However California law at that time prohibited such activity and narcotics agents raided the club in August 1996. The state obtained a court order closing the club.
At the time state Attorney General Dan Lungren's office accused the club of routinely selling marijuana to children and to people with forged doctors' notes or with no medical justification.
Three months later Californians passed a measure allowing sick people and their "primary caregiver" to legally possess and grow marijuana for medical use when recommended by a doctor.

"I don't think you or I are going to say the people of California were totally ineffectual" in passing the law, Garcia told lawyers for the state and the club at a hearing on Wednesday, granting the club's request to amend the order. But he said the club had to operate without making a profit or it would violate the law.
State lawyers argued the club should not be allowed to reopen because it was not a primary caregiver as required by the law.
The Clinton administration said marijuana remained an illegal drug under federal law and that it will sanction doctors who prescribe marijuana in California.

"I'm feeling so elated. Democracy prevails," club founder Dennis Peron said. "The war on marijuana is over today, mark my word," he added. Peron said the club would reopen on January 15 under a new name, the San Francisco Cannabis Cultivators' Club.

Peron said Garcia's decision allowed the club "to cultivate marijuana not only for ourselves but for others who designate us as caregiver and to distribute it in an orderly manner without profit. We intend to do that," he said.
Users must assign the club as caregiver, sign an affidavit that they would only use the drug for medicinal purposes and have a doctor's recommendation, he said.
Peron and five other alleged operators of the Cannabis Buyers' Club were charged in October 1996 with selling marijuana.

Lungren spokesman Steve Telliano said the state was considering appealing Garcia's ruling to seek guidance from higher courts on the meaning of "primary caregiver" in the measure because he said this had caused confusion.
